A.explanation: Gives half the correct value, from using $1$ cm for one period instead of the measured $2$ cm for one full sine wave.

B.explanation: Period $40 \text{ ms}$ divided by $2$ cm per cycle gives $20 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Confuses the $25 \text{ Hz}$ frequency number with a time-base value in $\text{ms cm}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Uses the full $40 \text{ ms}$ period as the time for $1$ cm, ignoring that one cycle spans $2$ cm.

hints: Notice the input frequency is $25 \text{ Hz}$, so first work out the period $T = 1/f$ in $\text{ms}$.
Look along the horizontal time axis and measure how many cm one complete sine wave occupies - check where the trace repeats.
Connect the two with time-base = period divided by horizontal length of one cycle in cm.
walkthrough: Find the period of the signal from $T = 1/f$. With $f = 25 \text{ Hz}$, $T = 1/25 = 0.040 \text{ s} = 40 \text{ ms}$.
Measure one full cycle on the trace. The repeating sine wave occupies $2$ cm horizontally per wavelength.
Recall the time-base setting is the time represented by $1$ cm horizontally, so time-base $= T / \text{length of one cycle}$.
Substitute values with units: time-base $= 40 \text{ ms} / 2 \text{ cm} = 20 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$.
This matches the $20 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ value. This is option B.
